cohort: The study included 530 full-term pregnant women who underwent primary cesarean delivery.
finding: Despite similar niche incidence, the double-layer uterine closure technique showed superior benefits at 6 and 12 months post-cesarean delivery, with greater residual myometrial thickness, better healing, and smaller niche volumes, although niche volume itself significantly increased over time.
mod_finding: The double-layer uterine closure technique during cesarean delivery resulted in superior outcomes, including greater residual myometrial thickness and smaller niche volume, compared to the single-layer technique.
